# apicp_firewall_site (Resource)

A connection on a dynamic address (an office or home whose ISP renumbers it), kept as a DNS name that follows it (dynamic DNS, or any name you keep pointing at it). Its current addresses are let through every restricted port of the firewall (or only the listed `ports`), on top of each `apicp_firewall_restriction`'s own sources, and the firewall is re-applied when the name's address changes (checked every minute, `APICP_FIREWALL_REFRESH`; a lookup that fails keeps the last address). A restriction may then list no source of its own: "SSH from my sites only". A port restricted to sites whose names have not resolved yet stays closed, never open. Sites count for the lockout guard. Anything that can write to the name can open the firewall to its address: use a dynamic DNS account you control. Import with the site id.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "apicp_firewall" "this" {}

# The office is on an ISP that renumbers it; b.example.org follows it (dynamic DNS).
resource "apicp_firewall_site" "office" {
  name = "Office"
  host = "b.example.org"
}

# Home reaches SSH and the API only.
resource "apicp_firewall_site" "home" {
  name  = "Home"
  host  = "v.example.org"
  ports = [22, 8080]
}

# SSH from the sites only: no address of its own. Until a site's name has
# resolved, the port stays closed rather than open.
resource "apicp_firewall_restriction" "ssh" {
  depends_on = [apicp_firewall.this, apicp_firewall_site.office, apicp_firewall_site.home]
  port       = 22
  sources    = []
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `host` (String) The DNS name that follows the connection (or a fixed address).
- `name` (String) A label, unique among sites.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean)
- `ports` (Set of Number) Restrict the site to these firewall ports (22, 8080, 143...). Empty is every restricted port.

### Read-Only

- `addresses` (Set of String) What the name resolves to now.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import apicp_firewall_site.office site-0123abcd
```
